Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call today — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of discovery:
- Primary use case: customer support agent assistant that ingests user messages and returns suggested responses.
- Primary concerns: PII in request/response logs (emails, SSNs, payment details), headers containing tokens/trace IDs, and data residency for EU accounts.
- Retention target: FintechCo prefers 90 days for hosted logs; longer retention needs export to your S3.

What we can provide today:
- Redwood can provide configurable logging profiles: persist full requests, redact specified fields, or never persist user request bodies.
- Header capture is configurable; we can mask or drop specific headers (e.g., Authorization, X-Trace-ID).
- Out-of-the-box PII redaction (email, SSN, CC numbers) plus custom regex masks.
- For data residency: logs can be routed to your EU bucket (S3/GCS) or disabled in hosted environment.

Requested deliverables / next steps:
1) I attached a short brief (redwood-logging-controls-brief.pdf) that summarizes options — please review.
2) Dev (cc'd) will follow up with technical notes and sample configs for your engineers.
3) Can we schedule a 30-min technical sync this week with your security team to walk controls and SOC2 evidence? Suggested slots: Wed 6/24 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 6/25 09:00-11:00 PT.

Please confirm which time works or propose alternative. Also flag any specific headers or fields you want masked in the example configs.

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifying Qs before we schedule the technical call: 

1) By default, does Redwood persist full request/response bodies in hosted logs? For our PII policy we prefer request bodies not be stored unless explicitly opted-in.
2) Are HTTP headers (including X-Trace-ID, user-agent, Authorization-like headers) stored by default? Can we configure which headers are captured vs dropped?
3) We need deterministic masking for trace IDs so they can still be used for dedup/trace correlation without exposing the raw ID. Can you support hashing/consistent tokenization?
4) Retention: you mentioned routing logs to our EU bucket — what is the pipeline and how long until exported logs are available? Can we set retention to exactly 90 days and have automatic purge?
5) SOC 2: do you have a redacted SOC 2 report or evidence pack we can share with internal auditors?

Alex — perfect questions, thanks. High-level answers below; I've asked Dev to add the technical config examples and confirm details on hashing/trace handling.

- Default persistence: For hosted customers, Redwood captures request metadata by default but request/response bodies are NOT persisted unless the customer enables the "persist_bodies" logging profile. For default accounts we can set the account to "no-persist" so bodies are never stored.
- Headers: Capture is configurable. We can include a permitted-list or block-list for headers. Common pattern: drop Authorization, mask X-Client-Token and hash X-Trace-ID.
- Trace IDs: We support consistent hashing (HMAC with account key) so same trace ID maps to same hash — usable for correlation but not reversible.
- Retention/export: We support configurable retention windows (30/90/365) in the console. Exports to customer S3/GCS happen via an async export job (near-real-time, typically <5 minutes) and can be configured for EU buckets. Purge policies run after the retention window.
- SOC 2: we can provide a redacted SOC 2 summary and evidence bundle; Dev will attach the summary and a pointer to our compliance docs.

Proposed next step: Dev — can you post the tech notes and sample config snippets (masking regex, example HMAC config for trace IDs) and confirm whether any of the above would require Dedicated or Private deployment?

If Wed 6/24 10:00 PT works for you and Priya, I'll place a calendar invite.

Thanks,
--
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechco.com>

Subject: FintechCo - technical notes: logging, masking, and retention

Hi Alex / Priya — following up with technical details as promised. Pasting the key config patterns and behaviors below; attaching a more detailed tech note and our SOC2 summary.

1) Persistence behavior (hosted):
- logging_profile: "no-persist" => request and response bodies are never written to disk or object storage. Only metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts) are kept.
- logging_profile: "metadata-only" => request metadata + selected headers retained; bodies omitted.
- logging_profile: "full" => full request/response retained (opt-in only).

2) Header capture / masking:
- header_whitelist: ["content-type", "user-agent"]
- header_blacklist: ["authorization", "cookie"]
- header_mask_rules: [{"header": "x-client-token", "mask": "^(.{4}).*(.{4})$"}, {"header": "x-email", "mask": "email_redact"}]
- Masking supports regex-based substitution and named token types (email, ssn, cc).

3) Trace ID handling:
- Option A (masked): drop X-Trace-ID entirely from persisted logs.
- Option B (hashed): use per-account HMAC (SHA256) with a configurable salt to generate deterministic, non-reversible IDs. Example: trace_hash = HMAC_SHA256(account_key, raw_trace_id).
- Option C (tokenized): replace raw ID with a stable UUID mapped in an ephemeral store (not persisted beyond session).

4) PII detection and redaction:
- Built-in detectors: email, SSN (US), credit-card patterns, phone numbers.
- Custom regex rules supported for domain-specific tokens (customer ids, account numbers).

5) Retention and data residency:
- retention_days: integer (30/90/365). After retention period, logs are automatically purged from Redwood-hosted stores.
- export_sink: s3://fintechco-logs-eu/ (supported) — exports are streamed via our secure transfer job; typical latency <5 minutes.
- For absolute residency: customer-managed Dedicated/Private deployments can keep logs entirely within customer VPC/storage.

6) SOC 2 / compliance artifacts:
- Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (redacted summary) and a short tech-note (redwood-logging-controls-tech-notes.pdf) with sample policies and HMAC guidance. We can coordinate an NDA/redacted bundle if your audit team needs more detail.

If you want, I can join the call Wed 6/24 10:00 PT to walk through the sample configs and help your engineers test the masking rules against sample payloads. Please share a test payload (sanitized) or fields to mask and I'll prepare a small demo.

Thanks,
